primitives.name: Fenwick Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: Fenwick rating (shots plus missed shots) and Corsi rating (shots, missed shots, blocked shots) have been used to analyze players and teams because they have been shown to be better than goals as a predictor of future goals.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{\\text{fenwick}}': 'dimensionless count of shots and missed shots per game'}
primitives.assumptions: Shot attempts are independent and identically distributed; goal-scoring is stochastic but predictable via shot volume.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Low-scoring environments where goal variance dominates shot variance.

layer2.mapping: Fenwick differentials serve as input features for expected goal regression models in GSI; used in GSE for possession-state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between Fenwick differential and future goal differential.

primitives.name: Corsi Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: Fenwick rating (shots plus missed shots) and Corsi rating (shots, missed shots, blocked shots) have been used to analyze players and teams because they have been shown to be better than goals as a predictor of future goals.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_{\\text{corsi}}': 'dimensionless count of shots, missed shots, and blocked shots per game'}
primitives.assumptions: All shot events contribute equally to territorial control; blocked shots reflect defensive pressure.

primitives.name: Expected Goals Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: We use ridge regression to estimate a player's contribution to his team's _expected_ goals per 60 minutes, independent of his teammates, opponents, and the zone in which his shifts begin.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{EG}': 'expected goals per 60 minutes (dimensionless)', '\\beta_0': 'intercept term (dimensionless)', '\\beta_i': 'regression coefficients (dimensionless)', 'X_i': 'predictor variables (shots, hits, faceoffs, etc.)', '\\lambda': 'ridge penalty parameter (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear relationship between predictors and expected goals; multicollinearity mitigated by ridge regularization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sample size is insufficient or predictors are highly correlated.

layer2.mapping: Expected goals map to GSI's probabilistic player evaluation; GSE uses them for state-space dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error of predicted vs. actual goals across seasons.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper lies in replacing goal counts—a sparse, high-variance outcome—with more frequent and stable proxies like shots, misses, and blocks. Fenwick and Corsi ratings capture the essence of possession pressure without relying on rare goal events. These metrics are then embedded into a linear regression framework augmented with ridge regularization to prevent overfitting. The resulting expected goals (EG) model estimates a player’s offensive contribution per 60 minutes, controlling for teammates/opponents and zone effects. This allows for robust comparisons across contexts. The failure mode arises when predictors are collinear or when data is too limited to support the complexity of the model. Additionally, the model assumes that past performance correlates with future outcomes, which may not hold during major roster changes or rule modifications.
